title: Shelly
desc: Smart relays, plugs and energy meters

pages.t: Shelly is made by Shelly Group (earlier called Allterco), with roots in Sofia, Bulgaria. It also has offices in Munich and other countries, and is present in over 100 markets. The shares are listed on stock exchanges, so this is an established company, not a startup.
g: Smart home
Home devices you control from a phone or automate: lights, heating, shutters, plugs.
Listed company
A company whose shares are traded on a stock exchange.

pages.t: Shelly makes small smart relays and switches, dimmers, plugs, sensors, thermostats, energy meters and more. There is also a professional line and a Bluetooth sensor line. The idea is one family of devices for lights, heating, shutters and energy.
g: Relay
An electronic switch that turns a power circuit on or off when told to.
Energy meter
A device that measures how much electricity is used or produced.

pages.t: Shelly works with official resellers and verified installers. Allnet Nordic is a distributor: we supply resellers and installers, who then sell to home owners and businesses. Your customer is the electrician or installer, not the person living in the house.
g: Distributor
A company that buys from the vendor and sells to resellers, not to end users.
Installer
A professional, often an electrician, who fits and sets up systems for customers.

quiz.q: Where does Shelly come from?
quiz.w: Shelly Group has its roots in Sofia, Bulgaria, and also has offices in Munich and other places.

quiz.q: Who is Allnet Nordic's typical Shelly customer?
o: A home owner buying one plug
quiz.w: Allnet is a distributor. Resellers and installers buy from us and sell on to end customers.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT something Shelly is known for?
quiz.w: Shelly makes smart home and energy devices. Firewalls are a different world, such as Stormshield.

pages.h: It fits behind the wall switch
pages.t: Many Shelly relays are tiny. The Plus 1PM is about 37 x 42 x 16 mm and is small enough for many wall boxes, behind an existing switch or socket. So you can make an old house smart without new wall panels or new cables.
g: Retrofit
Adding smart features to an existing building without major rebuilding.
Wall box
The small box in the wall that holds a switch or socket.

pages.t: Shelly devices join the normal Wi-Fi or network and need no extra hub box. A Plus device can run on the local network without the internet, using its built-in web page. Remote access through the Shelly cloud is optional.
g: Hub
A central box that other smart devices must connect to before they work.
Local control
Controlling a device over your own network, without a vendor's internet service.

pages.t: Shelly lists support for Alexa, Google Home, Apple HomeKit, Matter and Home Assistant. Home Assistant states that its Shelly integration talks directly to the device and needs no cloud. That means little vendor lock-in for the installer.
g: Home Assistant
A popular free smart home platform that people run themselves.
Lock-in
Being stuck with one vendor because nothing else works with their products.
Matter
A common smart home standard so devices from different brands work together.

quiz.q: Why can a Shelly Plus 1PM often go behind an existing light switch?
quiz.w: The Plus 1PM is only about 37 x 42 x 16 mm, so it often fits a wall box.

quiz.q: What does 'no hub required' mean for the installer?
o: Fewer boxes to buy and set up
It only works with one app
quiz.w: Shelly devices connect to the normal network directly, so there is no extra central box to buy.

quiz.q: An installer worries about being locked to one vendor's app. Best Shelly argument?
o: It only works in the Shelly cloud
Local control and integrations such as Home Assistant
quiz.w: Shelly can run locally and integrates with many platforms, so the customer is not forced into one cloud.

pages.h: The relay is the core product
pages.t: A relay sits in the wall box and switches a lamp, pump or other load. Plus 1 is one channel. Plus 1PM adds power measurement, so you can see how much the connected load uses.
g: Load
The thing that is switched, such as a lamp, pump or heater.
PM
Power Metering: the device measures power use as well as switching.
Channel
One independent output a relay can switch.

pages.t: The Plus 2PM has two channels with power metering. It can switch two separate circuits or work in cover mode to drive a roller shutter, blind or awning. One product covers both jobs, which keeps stocking simple.
g: Roller shutter
A window cover that rolls up and down, driven by a motor.

pages.t: The Plus i4 has four inputs and no output. It reads wall buttons or switches and uses them to trigger scenes or control other Shelly devices. Use it when a wall button should start something elsewhere, not switch its own load.
g: Scene
A saved set of actions, such as all lights off, triggered by one press.

quiz.q: What does the 'PM' in Plus 1PM add?
quiz.w: PM stands for power metering: the device measures how much the connected load uses.

quiz.q: A customer wants to control a roller shutter. Which fits?
quiz.w: The 2PM has a cover mode for shutters and blinds. The i4 has no outputs and the H&T is a sensor.

quiz.q: What is the Plus i4 for?
o: Reading wall buttons to trigger other things
quiz.w: The i4 only has inputs. It turns button presses into actions for other devices.

quiz.q: Which statement is true for the Plus 2PM?
quiz.w: The 2PM has two channels with metering, usable for two circuits or one cover motor.

pages.t: The Plus Plug S is a smart plug with built-in power measurement and overheating protection. It needs no installation: plug it in, plug the appliance in. Good for a heater or a coffee machine, or for checking what an old appliance really uses.
g: Smart plug
An adapter that sits between socket and appliance and can switch it remotely.

pages.t: The Plus H&T is a battery sensor with a screen that reports temperature and humidity. It runs on 4 AA batteries, about a year according to the manual. Its readings can be sent to other systems, for example via webhooks or MQTT.
g: Sensor
A device that measures something, like temperature, motion or light.

pages.h: EM Gen3: a small energy meter
pages.t: The Shelly EM Gen3 measures a single phase using external current clamps, described as contactless metering. It is small enough for a wall box. Use it to see what a circuit or a whole home uses.
g: Phase
One of the live wires in mains power; homes have one or three.
Current clamp (CT)
A clip-on sensor that measures current without cutting the wire.

quiz.q: A retailer wants a no-installation device to see what an appliance uses. Which?
quiz.w: The Plug S has built-in power measurement and needs no wiring.

quiz.q: What does the Plus H&T measure?
quiz.w: H&T stands for humidity and temperature.

quiz.q: What does the EM Gen3 use to measure current?
quiz.w: It measures through external CTs, described as contactless metering.

pages.t: The Pro line is made for the DIN rail inside the fuse cabinet. Models include Pro 1, 1PM, 2, 2PM, 3 and 4PM, plus dimmers and energy meters. Pro devices such as the 4PM and 3EM offer LAN (Ethernet), Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
g: DIN rail
A standard metal rail in electrical cabinets that devices clip onto.
LAN / Ethernet
A wired network cable connection, generally more stable than Wi-Fi.

pages.t: Professional jobs often want everything in one cabinet with a wired network connection, which is generally more stable than Wi-Fi. The Pro 4PM has four channels, and a colour screen with buttons on the front for local menus.
g: Cabinet
The fuse or distribution box where circuits are protected and switched.

pages.t: Rule of thumb: Plus goes behind switches in existing homes, Pro goes in the cabinet for larger or professional jobs. Both are Shelly, so the same family and way of working. Pro 3EM is the three-phase energy meter of the Pro range.
g: Three-phase
Mains supply with three live wires, common in larger buildings.

quiz.q: Where is a Shelly Pro device normally mounted?
o: On a DIN rail in the cabinet
quiz.w: Pro devices are DIN-rail products for electrical cabinets.

quiz.q: What connection do Pro devices offer that is useful in a cabinet?
quiz.w: Pro devices such as the 4PM offer wired LAN as well as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

quiz.q: Customer: an old house, only a wall box behind the switch, no cabinet space. Which line?
quiz.w: Plus relays are made to sit in the wall box behind existing switches.

src.l: Enabling Matter on Shelly Gen3 and newer

pages.t: Shelly numbers its device generations. Plus and Pro belong to Gen2. Gen3 and Gen4 follow. Shelly says the Gen2 generation brought a faster processor and more memory, and unified settings across devices.
g: Generation (Gen)
A hardware and software version of the product family; newer is generally more capable.
Firmware
The software inside a device; it can be updated.

pages.t: The Shelly knowledge base explains how to enable Matter on Gen3 and newer devices that do not have it by default. It needs a firmware update and a Matter hub. Check the exact model before promising Matter, because support can differ.
g: Matter
A shared smart home standard, so devices from different brands work together.
Hub
A central box that links devices.

pages.t: Gen4 was presented in 2025 with multi-protocol connectivity: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Matter or Zigbee, switchable per device. Mini models are extra small relays for tight wall boxes. In short: pick the newest generation that fits the job.
g: Zigbee
A low-power wireless standard used by many smart home sensors and lights.
Multi-protocol
One device that can speak several wireless languages.

quiz.q: Which generation do the Plus and Pro lines belong to?
quiz.w: Plus and Pro devices belong to Gen2.

quiz.q: A customer asks about Matter. Best answer?
o: All Shelly ever made supports it
Newer generations can support it, check the exact model
quiz.w: Matter is available on Gen3 and newer, but support depends on the model and firmware.

quiz.q: What is a Shelly Mini?
quiz.w: Mini devices are the extra-compact relays for tight wall boxes.

lessons.title: BLU: Bluetooth sensors and the gateway

pages.t: BLU is Shelly's range of small Bluetooth devices: motion sensor, door and window sensor, temperature sensor, buttons, remotes and a radiator valve (TRV). They are battery powered and need no wiring, so they suit retrofits.
g: Bluetooth LE
A low-power short-range wireless link used by small battery devices.
TRV
Thermostatic radiator valve: a smart valve on a radiator that regulates room heat.

pages.t: BLU devices talk Bluetooth, not Wi-Fi, so they need a gateway to reach the Wi-Fi network. The BLU Gateway Gen3 is a Bluetooth-to-Wi-Fi unit with a USB-A connector. It supports up to five BLU TRVs, with a range of up to 10 m indoors.
g: Gateway
A device that connects two kinds of network, here Bluetooth and Wi-Fi.

pages.t: The BLU Motion sensor runs on one coin battery, which Shelly estimates at up to 5 years. In the Shelly app it needs a powered Shelly Wi-Fi and Bluetooth device, Gen2 or newer, acting as the gateway. So an existing Shelly relay can sometimes do that job.
g: Coin cell
A flat round battery, like the ones in watches and key fobs.

quiz.q: What wireless technology do BLU devices use?
quiz.w: BLU stands for Bluetooth devices, which are battery powered and wire-free.

quiz.q: A customer wants smart radiator valves in an old building. What do you offer?
o: BLU TRV with a BLU Gateway Gen3
quiz.w: The BLU TRV is the radiator valve, and it reaches the network through a gateway.

quiz.q: Why does a BLU sensor need a gateway to reach your network?
quiz.w: The gateway bridges Bluetooth to the Wi-Fi network.

quiz.q: How many TRVs can one BLU Gateway Gen3 handle?
quiz.w: The Gen3 gateway page says it supports up to five BLU TRVs.

pages.h: Two ways to use the same device
pages.t: Shelly devices can be controlled locally on your own network or remotely through the Shelly cloud. Plus devices run on a local Wi-Fi network with a built-in web page, and they also work with cloud services for remote access.
g: Cloud
Internet servers run by a vendor, used for remote access and sharing.

pages.t: The Shelly app sets up devices, schedules and scenes. Shelly also offers a paid Premium tier with extra features. As a seller you mostly need to know that Premium is an optional add-on for the end user, not something the installer must sell.
g: Subscription
A recurring fee for extra features or services.

pages.t: Shelly devices offer open interfaces such as MQTT and HTTP, and scripts that run inside the device. Home Assistant uses the device directly, no cloud needed. Integrators like this because they can build their own dashboards and rules.
g: MQTT
A light messaging protocol used by many smart home systems.
API
A way for other software to talk to a device in a defined way.

quiz.q: Can a Shelly Plus device run without the cloud?
o: No, it always needs the cloud
quiz.w: The Plus devices run standalone on a local Wi-Fi network through their web interface.

quiz.q: What is Shelly Premium?
quiz.w: Shelly offers a paid Premium tier in the app with extra features.

quiz.q: An integrator wants to build own automations with open interfaces. What helps?
quiz.w: Shelly devices offer MQTT, HTTP and scripting for custom setups.

pages.t: The Pro 3EM is a DIN-rail three-phase meter. Current clamps (CTs) go on the incoming cables. It shows voltage, current and power per phase, and stores data at one-minute intervals for at least 45 days.
g: Three-phase meter
A meter that measures all three live wires of a mains supply separately.

pages.t: Shelly calls the Pro 3EM photovoltaic ready: it measures energy flowing in both directions, import and export. That lets you compare solar production with grid use. Choose by current range: 120 A clamps on the Pro 3EM, or the Pro 3EM-400 for up to 400 A.
g: Photovoltaic (PV)
Solar panels that turn sunlight into electricity.
Import / export
Energy taken from the grid versus fed back into it.

pages.t: Shelly suggests a home energy profiling service: leave a Pro 3EM at the main board for two to four weeks, then show the customer their usage to help size a solar system. Do not promise it replaces the grid company's official meter.
g: Profiling
Recording usage over time to see patterns.
Billing meter
The official meter the grid company uses to charge you.

quiz.q: What can the Pro 3EM tell a customer about solar?
o: How many panels fit the roof
Energy flowing both ways, import and export
quiz.w: It is photovoltaic ready with measurement of energy in both directions.

quiz.q: A big site needs clamps up to 400 A. Which model?
quiz.w: The Pro 3EM-400 is the version listed for 400 A current transformers.

quiz.q: What is the idea behind energy profiling?
o: Measure usage for weeks to help size solar
quiz.w: The meter records usage so the installer can advise on a suitable solar system.

quiz.q: Do we promise the Pro 3EM replaces the grid company's billing meter?
quiz.w: Shelly presents it as a monitoring and profiling tool, so never promise it replaces the official meter, and check local rules.

pages.t: First ask: where does it go and what must it do? Behind a switch: Plus or Mini relay. In the cabinet: Pro. Battery sensor or radiator valve: BLU. Whole-house energy: Pro 3EM. Anywhere, no tools: a plug.

• Radiator valve: BLU TRV plus BLU Gateway
  • DIN-rail install: Pro 4PM or another Pro relay
  • Measure solar and grid: Pro 3EM
  • Roller shutter: Plus 2PM in cover mode
Before quoting, confirm load size (the 1PM handles 16 A, the 2PM 10 A per channel), whether a neutral wire is present, and Wi-Fi coverage. Ask the installer: they know the site and the local rules.
g: Neutral wire
The return wire in mains power; some smart devices need it in the wall box.

quiz.q: A customer wants to automate a heating radiator valve. Which?
o: BLU TRV with a BLU Gateway
quiz.w: The BLU TRV is the smart radiator valve and uses the gateway to reach the network.

quiz.q: Fuse cabinet install with several circuits and a wired network. Which?
quiz.w: The Pro 4PM is a DIN-rail relay with four channels and LAN.

quiz.q: Measure solar output and grid use on a three-phase site. Which?
quiz.w: The Pro 3EM measures per phase in both directions.

quiz.q: A customer wants quick power data on one appliance, no wiring. Which?
quiz.w: The Plug S is plug and play and measures power use.

src.l: Smart Home Compared: Fibaro vs Shelly

pages.t: Smart home relays come in types: Wi-Fi relays like Shelly, Z-Wave systems like Fibaro that work with a controller, and big building systems. Shelly aims at adding smart control behind existing switches and outlets.
g: Z-Wave
A low-power wireless standard that works with a Z-Wave controller or hub.
Controller
The brain of a smart home system that links devices and runs rules.

pages.t: A review comparison says Shelly suits people who want smart control behind existing switches, with broad integration with Home Assistant, Alexa and Google Home. Shelly also lists Z-Wave, Zigbee and KNXnet/IP in its range, so it can meet other worlds.
g: KNX
A wired professional building automation standard.

pages.t: 'Is it only for hobbyists?' Point to the Pro line, DIN rail and wired LAN. 'What if the cloud goes away?' Local control. 'Is it locked in?' Open interfaces and integrations. Be honest on limits: check load size and Matter support per model.
g: Objection
A concern or doubt a customer raises before buying.

quiz.q: Which is a typical difference between Fibaro and Shelly?
o: Fibaro is Z-Wave based and uses a controller
quiz.w: The comparison describes Fibaro as Z-Wave based, while Shelly adds control behind existing switches.

quiz.q: 'Shelly is just for hobbyists.' Best answer?
o: Point to the Pro line for professional installs
quiz.w: The Pro line is DIN-rail and wired for professional jobs.

quiz.q: A customer fears cloud dependence. What do you say?
o: Devices can run locally without the cloud
quiz.w: Shelly devices can be controlled locally on the network.

lessons.title: Who buys and what to ask

pages.t: Typical buyers are electricians and installers who retrofit homes, integrators who build full smart systems, and retailers who sell plug-and-play items like plugs and sensors. Shelly works with official resellers and verified installers.
g: Integrator
A company that combines products from different brands into one working system.

pages.t:
• New build or existing home?
  • Behind switches or in a cabinet?
  • Do you need energy data or solar?
  • Which platform do end customers use: Alexa, Google, Apple or Home Assistant?

Energy gives extra business: a home energy profiling service with a Pro 3EM needs little training, according to Shelly. Combine relays with sensors and a gateway. Shelly also offers an Academy for training. Follow up with questions, not pressure.
g: Upsell
Selling an additional product to the same customer.

quiz.q: Which customer is most likely to buy plug and play items?
quiz.w: Retailers sell plug and play items like plugs and sensors.

quiz.q: Best opening question to an installer?
quiz.w: New build versus retrofit steers the choice between Pro and Plus.

quiz.q: What extra service can an installer offer with a Pro 3EM?
quiz.w: Shelly suggests profiling a home's energy use over weeks to help size solar.

about: Bulgarian smart home brand from Shelly Group, earlier called Allterco, present in over 100 markets. Makes small relays, plugs, sensors, energy meters and a professional line.
Sold through resellers and verified installers, who add smart control to existing homes and buildings.
Different because it fits behind existing wall switches, needs no hub, can run locally without the internet and works with Home Assistant, Alexa and Google Home.
